lessons.culture: Visiting the sick (عيادة المريض) is a strong duty in Yemen, so hospital rooms fill with relatives and neighbours. Visitors say "ما تشوف شر" or "سلامات" and pray "الله يشفيه". Families often stay with the patient day and night and bring home-cooked food.

exercises.prompt: A relative asks: "متى يقدر يخرج من المستشفى؟" Say in two days, God willing.
exercises.tip: Add "إن شاء الله" when talking about the future.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "الحمد لله، هو بخير _____." (Praise be to God, he is fine now.)

too_formal.feedback: "الآن" is formal; say "ذلحين".

exercises.tip: "ذلحين" is the Sana'ani "now".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "_____ سيارة إسعاف." (I need an ambulance.)
exercises.tip: "أشتي" is "I want" or "I need" in Sana'a.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "My father had an accident."
exercises.tip: "وقع له" is "happened to him".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I'm worried about him." (a man speaking)
exercises.tip: A woman says "قلقانة".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "The operation will take two hours."

too_formal.feedback: This is formal; say "العملية عتطوّل ساعتين".

exercises.tip: For "he", "she" and "they", Sana'a marks the future with "عـ".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence tells a man to register the patient's name at reception?
exercises.tip: "سجّل" is "register!" to a man.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "I'll measure his temperature"?
exercises.tip: "شا" + "أقيس" gives "شاقيس".

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "في / يومين / يجلس / لازم / المستشفى".
exercises.tip: Start with "لازم" (he must).

challenge.title: A Visit to the Doctor and the Pharmacy
challenge.instructions: Write and act out a conversation of at least 10 lines where you tell a friend or a doctor how you feel, describe at least two symptoms using body-part words, and then go to the pharmacy to get medicine. Use at least 8 target phrases from Unit 9 and include both a masculine-address and a feminine-address form somewhere in your conversation.
required_elements: A question about how someone feels, like كيفك or إيش سار فيك.
At least two symptoms named with body-part words, such as راسي or بطني.
A mention of حرارة or صداع or another specific complaint.
A question asking since when the person has felt this way, using من إيمتى.
A pharmacy or doctor request using عندك or أشتي.
A question about a prescription using وصفة.
Instructions for taking medicine, such as مرتين باليوم.
A closing wish using سلامتك and its reply الله يسلمك.

dialogue.speaker: محمود
dialogue.arabic: السلام عليكم يا فاطمة، إيش فيك؟ شكلك تعبانة
dialogue.transliteration: assalam 3alaikum ya Fatima, eesh feek? shaklak ta3baana
dialogue.english: Hi Fatima, what's wrong, you look tired

dialogue.speaker: فاطمة
dialogue.arabic: وعليكم السلام، عندي صداع وحرارة من يومين
dialogue.transliteration: wa 3alaikum assalam, 3indi soda3 w 7arara min yomeen
dialogue.english: Hi, I've had a headache and fever for two days

dialogue.speaker: محمود
dialogue.english: Since exactly when?

dialogue.speaker: فاطمة
dialogue.arabic: من يوم الخميس، وحلقي كمان يوجعني
dialogue.transliteration: min yoom il-khamees, w 7algi kamaan yooja3ni
dialogue.english: Since Thursday, and my throat hurts too

dialogue.speaker: محمود
dialogue.english: Go to the doctor, don't wait

dialogue.speaker: فاطمة
dialogue.arabic: إي، بروح ذلحين، وبعدين بمر على الصيدلية
dialogue.transliteration: ee, broo7 dhal7een. w ba3deen bamurr 3ala iS-Saydaliyya
dialogue.english: Yes, I'll go now. After that I'll stop by the pharmacy

dialogue.speaker: الدكتور
dialogue.english: What hurts you?

dialogue.speaker: فاطمة
dialogue.arabic: راسي وحلقي، وعندي حرارة من يومين
dialogue.english: My head and my throat, and I've had a fever for two days

dialogue.speaker: الدكتور
dialogue.arabic: ما في شيء خطير، بس لازم ترتاحي وبكتب لج وصفة
dialogue.transliteration: ma fi shay khaTeer, bas laazim tarta7i w biktub lich waSfa
dialogue.english: Nothing serious, but you need to rest and I'll write you a prescription

dialogue.speaker: فاطمة
dialogue.english: Thank you, doctor

dialogue.speaker: فاطمة
dialogue.arabic: السلام عليكم، عندك دوا حسب هالوصفة؟
dialogue.english: Hi, do you have medicine for this prescription?

dialogue.speaker: الصيدلاني
dialogue.arabic: إي تفضلي، خذيه مرتين باليوم بعد الأكل
dialogue.transliteration: ee tafaDDali, khidhiih mirrateen bilyoom ba3d il-akl
dialogue.english: Yes, take it twice a day after eating

dialogue.speaker: الصيدلاني
dialogue.english: Get well soon and goodnight

dialogue.speaker: فاطمة
dialogue.english: Thank you, thanks
